This website collects the material of the **Programming and Data Analysis
with R** part of the course *[Statistical Models and Applications in
Economics and Environmental Sciences]{.blue}*, B.Sc. in "*Economics and Science
for Environmental Sustainability*", Università degli Studi di
Milano-Bicocca.

The other module of the course, *Statistical Inference and Modeling*, is
not covered here.

::: callout-warning
#### Work in progress

This page is [under construction]{.blue}: the material is published as the
module progresses.
:::

## Teaching material

#### Required

- Agresti, A. and Kateri, M. (2022), *Foundations of Statistics for Data
  Scientists*, CRC Press.
- Agresti, A. and Kateri, M., [*R Web
  Appendix*](https://stat4ds.rwth-aachen.de/pdf/DS_R_webAppendix.pdf) of the
  above book. It is [freely available]{.orange} and it is an integral part of
  the material of this module.

The [website of the book](https://stat4ds.rwth-aachen.de/), where the
[data files](https://stat4ds.rwth-aachen.de/data/) used in the exercises are
also hosted.

#### Optional

- R Core Team, [*An Introduction to
  R*](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-intro.pdf).

#### Notes and R scripts

The code is [written live]{.orange} during the classes, following the R
scripts. The notes cover exactly the same material and are there for you
to [consult at any time]{.blue}, before or after the class.

The acronym **AK** refers to the book by Agresti and Kateri: the sections
numbered §A0, §A1, . . . are those of its [R web
appendix](https://stat4ds.rwth-aachen.de/pdf/DS_R_webAppendix.pdf).

## Exam

The exam is a written examination held in the computer lab, combining theoretical
questions, exercises and exercises in **R**, covering both parts of the
course. Students are required to execute **R** code in order to answer
some of the questions.

::: callout-tip
During the exam it is legitimate --- indeed, strongly recommended --- to
consult the **R** documentation.
:::

| Date             | Exam                          |
|------------------|-------------------------------|
| *No exams yet*   |                               |


## Software

-   **R** is open source and can be downloaded at
    <https://cloud.r-project.org>.
-   The use of **RStudio** is optional but strongly recommended:
    <https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/>.
-   The documentation of the **R** software is an integral part of the
    teaching material.
